subject: Pilot gating & MAP: commercial terms + exec sign-off needed
messages:
From: Anna Park <anna@crossplay.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot scope & MAP — timing and initial ask

Jordan — thanks for the demo last week. CrossPlay is excited to run a short pilot to validate latency and cost for our chat moderation feature.

High level asks:
- 6 week pilot (30k messages/month equivalent)
- Access to the streaming API + embeddings for evaluation
- A MAP with clear milestones for performance verification and a go/no-go at week 4

Commercial note: procurement is looking for a starter discount on list pricing tied to a 12-month commit if the pilot validates. Can you share an indicative MAP-based commercial? Also can you attach a sample MAP document and a pricing worksheet?

Thanks —
Anna
Anna Park
Head of Product, CrossPlay
anna@crossplay.com

-----Original Message-----

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Anna Park <anna@crossplay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot scope & MAP — timing and initial ask

Hi Anna — great to hear. Attached a draft MAP (CrossPlay_MAP_v1.pdf) and our working pricing model (pricing_model_v3.xlsx). Summary below: 

Proposed MAP / commercial structure (indicative):
- Pilot (6 weeks): hosted evaluation account at list rate, full telemetry.
- Milestone at week 4 (performance gate): pass = move to scale pilot + pilot extension clause.
- Commercial commitment: if CrossPlay signs a 12-month committed plan within 30 days of week-4 pass, we will offer a ramp discount schedule capped at 18% across the first 6 months, tied to:
  * Month 1: 8% off list (on committed spend)
  * Month 3: 12% off with 50% of committed volume reached
  * Month 6: 18% off with 80% of committed volume reached
- If CrossPlay prefers a guaranteed ARR commit instead of volume milestones, we can replace volume triggers with a fixed committed spend threshold.

Notes/conditions: any discount above 15% triggers VP/CFO approval per policy. We will need a short approval loop if procurement asks for a deeper concession.

I'll loop in Marissa to own the MAP build and Marissa — can you start a commercial packet for the approval thread (pricing rationale + finance impact table)?

Best,
Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0192

Attachments: CrossPlay_MAP_v1.pdf, pricing_model_v3.xlsx
From: Ben Lee <ben@crossplay.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Anna Park <anna@crossplay.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot scope & MAP — timing and initial ask

Thanks Jordan. Procurement ran the numbers and they are asking if we can push the up-front discount to 22% for the first two months and then step down to the ramp schedule you proposed. They argued that the initial cost to integrate and validate is material.

If that’s a non-starter, can we at least get a credit buffer (one month's credit) if the week-4 gate fails due to performance? Procurement would accept that as risk mitigation.

-Ben
Ben Lee
Head of Procurement, CrossPlay
procurement@crossplay.com
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Jun 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Pilot scope & MAP — CrossPlay discount ask (VP/CFO approval request)

Team — forwarding CrossPlay's updated ask. Key points: they want 22% off for months 1-2 (higher than our standard cap). They alternatively asked for a one-month credit if the week-4 gate fails.

Why this matters: CrossPlay is a strategic tackle partner for our gaming vertical; closing this pilot quickly keeps them in our regional partner program and opens marketplace placement. The economic impact (see attached pricing_model_v3.xlsx) would reduce billings in Q3 by an estimated $42k vs our standard ramp, but we expect higher CLTV if they hit commits.

Request: 
- Marcus / Neha: can you evaluate the 22% concession vs a one-month credit (attached quick P&L).
- Neha: if finance is OK with the 22% for 2 months tied to a hard volume/commit clause, we'd need VP/CFO sign-off per discount policy. If not, can you approve the one-month credit fallback?
- Marissa & Laura: please prepare concise talking points for procurement so we can close this week.

Attachments: pricing_model_v3.xlsx, redwood_contract_marked.docx

Thanks — Jordan

-----BEGIN FORWARDED MESSAGE-----
From: Ben Lee <ben@crossplay.com>

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pilot scope & MAP — CrossPlay discount ask (VP/CFO approval request)

Team — reviewed the packet and Marcus and I discussed the scenarios. Recommendation and approval:

1) Approve the one-month credit as primary fallback (no material change to our revenue recognition risk; credit applies only if week-4 gate fails attributable to Redwood).
2) Approve up to 18% blended discount across months 1–6 if CrossPlay signs a 12-month committed ARR with explicit volume milestones and a clawback for missed volume targets. 22% for months 1–2 is above tolerance and we should not approve that level.

Conditions:
- Legal to include a performance gate definition in the MAP and clawback language in the SOW.
- Sales to secure a signed commitment and the DocuSign envelope must be submitted within 30 days of week-4 pass.
- Finance will publish the final impact to bookings in the CP-2027-0012 HubSpot deal record.

Neha Kapoor
VP, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com
